name: phase1_nonzero_baseline
description: Is the +362 mW intercept a property of the all-zero operand, or does every
condition contrast carry a fixed offset?
phase1_hamming_weight fits dP = 0.362 + 0.0500*HW watts at R^2 = 0.974, but
dP(0) is zero by construction and its A/A confirms it at -14 mW. So the
curve has a step between HW 0 and HW 1: one set bit already buys 22% of the
full-range effect. Every contrast in that sweep used the all-zero operand as
its baseline, so the step could sit anywhere in the measurement.
Two readings, and they are not the same experiment:
A. The step belongs to HW 0. Moving all-zero data is anomalously cheap (or
the first set bit is anomalously expensive), and contrasts between two
non-zero operands should land on the 50 mW/bit line with no extra
offset. The sweep's numbers stand as measured, with the caveat that
they are all quoted against an unusually cheap baseline.
B. The step belongs to the contrast, not to zero: alternating a victim
between any two distinct working sets costs a fixed ~0.36 W. Then every
A/B result in this project is inflated by that amount, including the
traffic-volume depth table, and the A/A controls would not have caught
it because an A/A alternates between two conditions holding the *same*
value and so never swaps buffers.
Reading B is the reason this is worth 27 minutes. It is not excluded by
anything run so far.
Each run below contrasts two operands directly. Predictions are the
differences of the sweep's own per-pattern means, so under reading A each
measured value should match its prediction, and under reading B each should
exceed it by roughly the same ~0.36 W.
hw16_a -> hw16_b    +0.085 W      equal weight, different bits
0      -> hw16_a    +1.133 W      anchor, ties this session to the sweep
The A/A is on a non-zero operand this time. Every A/A run in this project so
far has held an all-zero or all-ones value; if anything about the zero
buffer is special, an A/A on it cannot show that either.
Driver settings match phase1_hamming_weight exactly so the anchor run is
directly comparable; the seeds differ.
